name: Kasa EP10

matter.note: TP-Link and Kasa list Alexa, Google and SmartThings (plus IFTTT) for the EP10, with no Matter.

apple_home.note: TP-Link's platform list for the EP10 (Alexa, Google Assistant, SmartThings) leaves out HomeKit, and it has no Matter.

google_home.note: Cloud-to-cloud link between the Kasa and Google accounts.

alexa.note: Cloud-to-cloud link via the Kasa skill.

smartthings.note: TP-Link lists Samsung SmartThings, and the user guide has SmartThings setup steps.

home_assistant.note: Listed by the official TP-Link Smart Home integration. One forum user reported EP10 units that weren't discovered.

hubRequired.note: Connects straight to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi; Kasa says no hub is required.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's integration controls Kasa plugs over the local network. The Kasa app itself goes through the cloud.

energyMonitoring.note: TP-Link's EP10 pages don't list a power meter, and a TP-Link community reply says it has none, but we found no official spec saying so.

maxLoadWatts.note: 15 A, 1800 W general use / resistive load at 100–120 V AC.

summary: The Kasa EP10 is a compact US Wi-Fi plug rated 15 A / 1800 W. It works with Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings through your Kasa account, with no hub, and Home Assistant's official TP-Link integration lists it. TP-Link doesn't list Apple Home or Matter for it.
caveats: No Apple Home or Matter support listed.
TP-Link doesn't advertise energy monitoring on this model; the EP25 is Kasa's metering version.
